record.question: The skeleton of which phyla is purely calcareous?
record.explanation: Held: the printed page 7 confirms the wording and all four options, but "purely calcareous" does not establish a unique answer. Gastropod and pelecypod shells both have calcium-carbonate mineral layers plus organic material; Bryozoa also include organic skeletons, so the phylum is not uniformly purely calcareous (see USGS, Chemical Composition of Ectoprocta: https://www.usgs.gov/publications/chemical-composition-ectoprocta-bryozoa). A restriction to a particular skeletal component or subgroup, or a corrected stem, is needed to choose uniquely.
